## **5\. Conclusion — When should AI be used (or not)?**

Based on the audit of five artifacts, clear patterns in AI performance emerged. AI shone at reading and analyzing large text documents, as seen in its accurate, "VALID" critiques of the 10 QA/QC job descriptions. However, AI failed when dealing with highly specific constraints and factual grounding. It hallucinated invalid source links and incorrect publication years for software defects, and generalized test cases for a specific Sharp rice cooker model by inventing unsupported features. It also struggled with precise formatting, producing text instead of a drawn mindmap and making grammatical errors in image generation. My recommendation for future work is to use AI for brainstorming, text summarization, and initial drafting, but to strictly avoid relying on it for factual data retrieval, URLs, or hardware-specific details without rigorous human auditing.
